cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: days from settlement to the next coupon date, semiannual, actual/actual
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 110. Setup serials are the dates Microsoft's page prints: 40568 = 2011-01-25 (settlement), 40862 = 2011-11-15 (maturity), frequency 2 (semiannual), basis 1 (actual/actual). Counting coupon dates back from maturity in six-month steps gives 2011-11-15, 2011-05-15, 2010-11-15, so the settlement date falls in the coupon period 2010-11-15 to 2011-05-15. On basis 1 the count is the actual number of days from 2011-01-25 to the next coupon date 2011-05-15, which Python date subtraction gives as 110. Consistency cross-check: 71 days before settlement + 110 days after = the 181-day period length COUPDAYS reports for the same bond

cases.description: The same bond paying annually instead of semiannually
cases.expected_note: With frequency 1 the coupon dates are 2011-11-15 and 2010-11-15, so the next coupon after the 2011-01-25 settlement is 2011-11-15 rather than 2011-05-15. The actual day count from 2011-01-25 to 2011-11-15 is 294 (Python date subtraction), which discriminates the frequency argument

cases.description: A day-count basis of 5, above the documented maximum of 4
